name: undo-list-limit-rejected
description: `-n` takes a value, which is why `undo` cannot find its snapshot id by scanning for the first token that is not a flag — under that rule `undo --list -n 3` would restore a snapshot called '3'. Here the value is rejected as a count (0 is not a number of snapshots to show) and the command exits 1 before touching the project, which is only reachable if `-n` consumed its own argument instead of leaking it into the id slot
